page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 7T83 cores running at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinct performance profile. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance metrics, such as the stress-ng multi-core test and Geekbench multi-core score, fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with both read and write operations on large blocks scoring in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression drops to the bottom 10%.

Given its compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2 and dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.c7a.xlarge offers an entry-level compute-focused profile. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated CPU execution but have low memory footprints. Due to weak database, redis, and multi-core performance, it is less suited for heavy database operations or high-throughput web serving. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded processing tasks, basic text processing, and lightweight single-core compute utilities.
